thinking: The analysis evaluates the House stopgap spending bill. Framed as a clean measure to avoid a government shutdown, the partisan nature of the bill and its lack of Senate viability reveal it as a strategic maneuver to shift blame, resulting in a trajectory of deception.
subject: House passes bill to fund the government through midterm elections
posts:
A funding fix or a pre-election blame game? The House passes a funding bill destined to die in the Senate.

House passes bill to fund the government through midterm elections
Evidence: Avoid shutdown, Partisan leverage, Blame shifting
#Aletheia #USPol

House Republicans claim the stopgap bill is a clean continuing resolution designed to fund the government through December and prevent a pre-election shutdown.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference

The bill is a partisan maneuver loaded with policy disputes, designed to fail in the Senate so Republicans can blame Democrats for any ensuing shutdown.
Resulting Judgement: (-1.0, 1.0) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
The bill is designed as a political weapon to shift blame rather than a viable bipartisan solution to keep the government open.

Integrity: Severe Deception (R_net: 12.5, Uncertainty z: 4)
House Republicans passed a stopgap funding bill to keep the government running into December. However, the bill lacks Senate support and faces opposition over partisan policy riders.

The Bright Side:
The vote temporarily forces lawmakers to put their positions on the record, clarifying party priorities ahead of the elections.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a HOW vs WHY error. The mechanism of passing a bill (HOW) is framed as a sincere effort to govern, but the underlying motive (WHY) is to secure electoral leverage.

Social Physics Analysis:
Instead of seeking a cooperative equilibrium, the strategy relies on creating a high-strain scenario. By passing a non-viable bill, the actors attempt to project the blame for future chaos onto their opponents.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. The partisan design ensures legislative failure.

The Unavoidable Truth: A bipartisan agreement is required to actually prevent a shutdown.

The Unavoidable Lie: This bill was passed with the sincere expectation of becoming law.

Alethekanon:
Passing a bill known to be dead on arrival in the upper chamber is not governance; it is performative legislative posturing designed to optimize campaign messaging.

Awwthekanon:
It is disheartening to see the stability of public services used as a bargaining chip. Real people rely on these programs, and they deserve cooperation, not conflict.

Brothekanon:
Another day, another shutdown showdown. Passing a bill you know is going to get trashed just to point fingers is peak DC behavior. Classic.
